focus.label: Post-encephalitic sequelae
focus.why: node-2 supports prior encephalitis and seizure history; node-5 supports cognitive sequelae; node-4 supports acquired non-genetic cause.

payload.query: Need the patient's brain MRI (or CT) and EEG reports: MRI can reveal post-encephalitic gliosis or scarring supporting sequelae, while EEG assesses epileptiform activity underlying seizures; these are essential to confirm the hypothesis and exclude an occult structural lesion.

payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of post-encephalitic sequelae, imaging reveals right cerebral hemisphere atrophy and encephalomalacia in the right frontal and temporal lobes on CT and MRI, consistent with prior encephalitis scarring; EEG shows right temporal slow waves without epileptiform discharges, supporting residual organic dysfunction rather than active epilepsy. These findings confirm an acquired structural sequelae and argue against migraine or anxiety as primary. All key imaging information is covered.
